sections.title: Letter sound
paragraphs: The Russian letter (дэ) /dɛ/ sounds like the sound /d/, that is a hard d. You hear it in the word (дом) /dom/, which means house. The letter makes four different sounds in Russian.

sections.title: Pronunciation
paragraphs: Press the tip of your tongue against the back of your upper teeth. Drop your tongue quickly as air breaks out, vibrating your vocal cords. For the second sound, press the flat top of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. The third sound moves like the first, but without your voice. The fourth sound moves like the second, but without your voice. Feel your throat vibrate for the first two sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: The letter sounds like the sound /d/, that is a hard d, before hard vowels. It makes this sound in the word (два) /dva/. Before soft vowels or a soft sign, it makes the sound /dʲ/, that is a soft d. You hear this sound in the word (день) /dʲenʲ/. At the end of a word, it sounds like the sound /t/, that is a hard t. This happens in the word (сад) /sat/. When softened at the end, it makes the sound /tʲ/, that is a soft t. You hear this in the word (медь) /mʲetʲ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not place your tongue behind your teeth as you do in the English word door. Touch your upper teeth directly. Do not puff out air like you do in the English word time. Keep the air release sharp and clean.
